newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Lumber won't cut U.S. redwoods for 14 days.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Lumber won't cut U.S. redwoods for 14 days.

text.p: Pacific Lumber Co. on Friday agreed not to cut down ancient redwoods in northern California for the next two weeks, allowing negotiations on a possible debt-for-nature swap to continue, a U.S. senator said.

"Promising negotiations toward an agreement in which the federal government and the state of California will acquire the Headwaters Forest are under way," said California Democrat Sen. Dianne Feinstein in a statement. "Pacific Lumber Company will not enter Headwaters Forest for two weeks while negotiations continue."

Clinton administration sources declined to give any further details on progress made in the negotiations. The two sides decided to take a break to observe the Jewish New Year holiday, and would resume talks on Monday, one source said.
"They've made enough progress to be able to continue," the source said.
Pacific Lumber, a unit of MAXXAM Inc, was due to begin taking downed trees in the Headwaters Grove in Humboldt County Monday, the only ancient redwood forest still held in private hands.
But the company has been negotiating with the government to exchange the 3,000 acres of virgin forest for surplus federal land or rights to harvest trees on other federal land.
